decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
This report provides an update on progress and
seeks further approvals for the acquisition of homes for temporary
accommodation delivered through the Local Authority Housing Fund.
It also proposes a strategic approach to securing long term (ten
years plus) leased accommodation through institutional and pension
fund backed providers to reduce reliance on nightly paid
accommodation and improve value for money.
content:
Cabinet is asked to:
 
A. Note the progress made in
acquiring homes to increase housing available to the Council to use
for temporary accommodation and reduce reliance on nightly paid
temporary accommodation.
B. Note that, in accordance
with his delegated powers, the Executive Director for Finance &
Digital signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of
Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) in March 2026 to
deliver Round 4 of the Local Authority Housing Fund (LAHF4), with
the sum of £15,081,000 to be spent on 62 homes across 4 four
years. A further £20,088,000 of council capital has been
allocated to support these acquisitions.
C. Approve the acquisition of a
proposed target of 125 homes during 2026/27 through a combination
of freehold purchase and long-term leasing arrangements.
D. Delegate to the Executive
Director of Housing & Sustainable Development in consultation
with the Executive Director for Finance and Digital and in
consultation with the Cabinet Members for Housing and Sustainable
Development and Finance and Corporate Services authority to acquire
properties which represent best value for the Council to achieve
the acquisition target of 125 homes for 2026/27, and where relevant
in accordance with the conditions of the Local Authority Housing
Fund.
E. Delegate authority to the
Executive Director of Housing & Sustainable Development in
consultation with the Cabinet Members for Housing and Sustainable
Development and Finance and Corporate Services into enter into any
contracts and deeds to acquire the units, and other legal
agreements required to facilitate the acquisitions and facilitating
of supply of the TA properties authorised by recommendation
D.
F. Note the criteria and
assumptions for the LAHF4 unit mix, which apply a portfolio
approach to the delivery of the programme and set indicative
purchase prices per property against each bedroom size. These
assumptions ensure the proposals in this report do not provide a
General Fund budget pressure and will be vetted and signed off by
the relevant executive directors, as set out in recommendation
D.
G. Consider the merits of
individual contractual arrangements of 10 years (or more) with
institutional and pension-fund backed providers on terms or similar
terms as set out in paragraph 4.46 to 4.51 of this report and,
subject to concluding any necessary procurement procedures, to
authorise the Executive Director of Housing & Sustainable
Development in consultation with the Cabinet Members for Housing
and Sustainable Development and Finance and Corporate Services to
enter into any contracts for the supply and use of these
units.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the acquisition of 125 homes to increase housing available for temporary accommodation and reduce reliance on nightly paid temporary accommodation.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
This report highlights progress toward
confirming the Article 4 Direction for small Houses in Multiple
Occupation (HMOs) across 13 wards in Merton. It outlines the
decision taken by Cabinet in February 2026 to introduce an
immediate borough-wide requirement for planning permission for new
HMOs, effective from March 2026. The report also explains the
statutory requirement to undertake public consultation and secure
formal confirmation of the Direction by September 2026 for it to
remain in force, and LSG’s views ahead of forthcoming Cabinet
and Council decisions.
content:
RESOLVED:
 
Cabinet is asked:
 
A. That, following review of
the consultation responses, Cabinet recommends to Council that the
immediate Article 4 Direction for small HMOs covering the 13 wards
listed in the report, which started on 24th March 2026, be
Confirmed to make it permanent.
 
B. To note that there is an
entitlement to compensation for the first 12 months where planning
permission is refused for development that would have been
permitted development but for an Article 4 Direction as set out in
the report.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to recommend making the immediate Article 4 Direction for small HMOs permanent in 13 wards.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Update on progress towards setting a balanced
budget for 2026/27. Review of MTFS and capital strategy
2026-30.
content:
RESOLVED:
 
A. That Cabinet considers and
agrees the response to the Overview and Scrutiny Committee
(Appendix 15)
 
B. That the Cabinet resolves,
having considered all of the information in this report, and noted
the Chief Financial Officer’s Section 25 statement provided
by the Executive Director, Finance and Digital, that it will freeze
the level of General Council Tax in 2026/27 and proposes an
increase of 2% in the Adult Social Care precept to help fund care
for older and vulnerable residents within Merton. This will equate
to a Band D Council Tax of £1,630.01, to be approved and
recommended to Council for approval.
 
C. That Cabinet considers
all of the latest information and the
comments from the scrutiny process, and makes recommendations to
Council as appropriate
 
D. That Cabinet resolves that
the Budget and Medium-Term Financial Strategy 2026-30 including the
General Fund Budget and Council Tax Strategy for 2026/27, and the
Medium-Term Financial Strategy (MTFS) for 2026-30 as submitted,
along with the Equality Impact Assessments (EIAs), be approved and
recommended to Council for approval subject to any proposed
amendments agreed at this meeting;
 
E. That Cabinet resolves that
having considered all of the latest information and the comments
from the scrutiny process, the Capital Investment Programme (as
detailed in Annex 3 to the Capital Strategy); the Treasury
Management Strategy, including the detailed recommendations in that
Section, incorporating the Prudential Indicators and the Capital
Strategy as submitted and reported upon, be approved and
recommended to Council for approval, subject to any proposed
amendments agreed at this meeting;
 
F. That Cabinet notes that the
GLA precept will not be agreed by the London Assembly until the 25
February 2025, but the provisional figure has been incorporated
into the MTFS.
 
G. That Cabinet request
officers to review the savings proposals agreed and where possible
bring them forward to the earliest possible implementation
date.
 
H. That Cabinet consider and
approve the Risk Management Strategy.
 
I. That Cabinet resolves that
the Council’s Strategy for the Flexible Use of Capital
Receipts 2025/30, as detailed in pages 26-28 of the Capital
Strategy be approved and recommended to Council for approval
subject to any proposed amendments agreed at this
meeting.
 
J. That Cabinet note that there
may be amendments to figures and words in this report as a result of new information being received after
the deadline for dispatch and that this will be amended for the
report to Council on 25 February 2026
K. That Cabinet note the report
commissioned from Peopletoo titled
“ Merton Council Financial
Healthcheck Review of Value for Money
& Critical Success Factors” attached as Appendix
16
topline: The Cabinet has decided to freeze the general council tax and propose a 2% increase in the Adult Social Care precept in Merton.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Paper on proposals relating to Article 4
Directions and Additional and Selective licensing schemes.
content:
Paper on proposals relating to Article 4
Directions and Additional and Selective licensing schemes.

RESOLVED:
 

A.   
That Cabinet reaffirms that one of Merton’s
key ambitions is to raise standards in the private rented sector
and continues its work on permitted development rights and landlord
licensing.

B.   
That Cabinet gives effect of having a borough-wide
Article 4 Direction for HMOs by introducing an immediate Directions
under Article 4 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted
Development) (England) Order 2015, withdrawing permitted
development rights for HMOs in all wards bar those already covered
by the 2022 Article 4 Direction.

C.  
That Cabinet agrees the resources and timeline to
extend selective and additional licensing schemes across the
borough.

D.  
That Cabinet approves the preparation for and making
of three non-immediate Directions under Article 4 of the Town and
Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order
2015, withdrawing permitted development rights for:
 
i.              
Town centres and neighbourhood
parades: conversion of ground floor
commercial, business and services uses
frontages to residential (Class MA) in the locations identified and
Class MA for offices (use class E(g)(i)
above ground floor in Wimbledon town centre
ii.             
Protected industrial areas: conversion of commercial, business and service uses (Class MA) in designated industrial estates to
residential
iii.            
Scattered employment sites: Class MA for office, research and development and light
industrial (Use Class E(g)) to residential (Class MA) on scattered
employment sites in the locations identified.
 

E.   
That Cabinet delegates authority to the Executive
Director of Housing and Sustainable Development to make the
arrangements, to include the public consultation, for the making of
the Article 4 Directions, selective and additional licensing, to
agree the final extent of the areas to which these will apply,
including if appropriate a further extension to Article 4 Direction
for HMOs and to waive enforcement action in relation to the
immediate Article 4 Direction on HMOs as set out in this
report.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to implement measures to raise standards in the private rented sector by introducing borough-wide Article 4 Direction for HMOs and extending selective and additional licensing schemes.

content:

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
This report seeks to update Members on actions
already being taken and obtain approval to pursue a series of
measures that will enable the Council to contribute directly to
addressing the housing crisis by enabling it to become a
self-deliverer of housing and in turn become a long-term stock
holding authority.
content:
RESOLVED:
 
Cabinet is asked to:
 
A. Note some of the measures
being taken to reduce the cost pressure to the Council of providing
Temporary Accommodation as set out in this Report.
B. Note the progress of the
investment made via Resonance in purchasing property to enable the
Council to discharge it homeless duty.
C. Approve the acquisition of
property for use as Temporary Accommodation both within and outside
the Borough as part of its response to the ongoing demand for
housing, subject to:
• the Executive Director
of Housing and Sustainable Development securing grant funding for
the acquisition(s) through bids submitted pursuant to
Recommendation D below;
• the full Council making
provision for the acquisition(s) in the Council’s budget of
c.£13m, medium term financial strategy and/or capital
investment programme (as appropriate);
• the properties targeted
for acquisition being fully in accordance with the terms of any
grant funding so secured and/or any Council funding provision so
made;
• the properties
satisfying any portfolio requirements including in relation to
property size, type, tenure, and/or purpose(s) contained in any
grant funding agreement(s) and/or Council funding provision;
• legal and property due
diligence having been completed satisfactorily; and
• the Executive Director
of Housing & Sustainable Development in conjunction with the
Executive Director of Finance & Digital and the Monitoring
Officer having determined that the Council’s best value duty
has been discharged.
D. Delegate to the Executive
Director of Housing & Sustainable Development, in conjunction
with the Executive Director of Finance & Digital and the
Monitoring Officer in accordance with the Council’s existing
budget and policy framework the acquisition of affordable housing
and temporary accommodation subject to the Acquisitions Board and
individual delegated authority reports.
E. Delegate to the Executive
Director of Housing & Sustainable Development authority to
submit bids to the Greater London Authority (GLA), Homes England
and the Ministry of Housing Communities and Local Government
(MHCLG) for funding to support the acquisition of properties for
use as Temporary Accommodation and to enter into any necessary
agreements to draw down such funding.
F. Note that contracts will be
let and work will commence on the development of 75 homes at Farm
Road, Raleigh Gardens and Elm Nursery Car Park.
G. Note the decision not to
proceed with the development at Canons Place at
this time, due to additional land becoming available,
allowing greater optimisation of the scheme.
H. Determine that the Council
should become a stock holding authority.
I. Approve a budget envelope
£500k to be funded on a one-off basis from reserves to allow
business planning and procedural processes to take place in
preparation for opening its Housing Revenue Account (HRA) pursuant
to becoming an HRA stock holding authority.
J. Note the work being
undertaken to explore opportunities for housing development on
Council land (section 5 of this Report) and to develop a Housing
Business Plan (section 6 of this Report).
K. Approve the preparation of a
Housing Delivery Business Plan and authorise officers to bring this
forward for Member approval.
L. Recognise the requirements
relating to a Housing Revenue Account (HRA) and approve the taking
of necessary steps with a view to re-establishing the HRA with
effect from the start of the 2027/28 financial year, subject to
subsequent approval by Members.
M. Approve the preparation of
an HRA budget and HRA capital programme in the context of the
long-term business plan and note officers will bring this forward
for Member approval.
N. Delegate to the Executive
Director of Housing and Sustainable Development to submit bids to
the Greater London Authority (GLA), Homes England and the Ministry
of Housing Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) for grant
subsidy to support the development and / or purchase of homes for
affordable housing provision.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve measures to reduce cost pressure, acquire properties for homeless duty, and develop affordable housing.
